- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.33) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast slightly, especially in early horizon.
- When sentiment is consistently negative (≤-0.33), model underestimates; adjust upward, particularly if recent price is falling sharply.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >5% from prior peak), model often overshoots in next 3–5 days; apply downward correction to avoid overreaction.
- If sentiment is neutral (0.00) for 3+ consecutive days, model tends to drift toward mean; apply mean-reversion bias toward recent 7–14 day average.
- For 30-day forecasts, model often overreacts to short-term sentiment shifts; smooth out extreme deviations by averaging with prior 14-day trend.
- If sentiment turns sharply positive after a negative trend, model may lag; anticipate upward correction in 3–7 days; adjust forecast upward by 1–2% of recent range.
- If sentiment is mixed (alternating +/–), model often fails to capture volatility; use sentiment-weighted moving average to dampen noise.
